```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

mirtverse gives you a complete, free set of materials for a course on item
response theory: A book, ten interactive labs, a 12-week course map, a
glossary and a cheat sheet. Everything is open, editable and runs on student
laptops.

## Your path in three steps

**1. See how the pieces fit a semester.** The [course map](course-map.html)
ties each week to a book chapter, a lab and a reading, and the
[sample syllabus](../adopt/mirtverse-sample-syllabus.docx) (Word) turns it
into a document you can edit and hand out.

**2. Try a lab the way your students will.** Each lab is a realistic case,
such as advising a certification board or investigating a fairness
complaint, with live mirt models and decisions to defend:

```r
library(mirtverse)
list_labs()                 # the ten labs
run_lab("fairness")         # Lab 3: Is the test fair?
```

The [Teaching labs](teaching-labs.html) article has the learning goals,
timing, discussion prompts and an answer key for each lab.

**3. Make it yours.** Build a lab on your own data, swap the dataset in a
built-in lab, or copy a book chapter to edit:

```r
new_course("irt-fall-2027")                    # a course folder
new_lab("my-lab", data = mydata, course = "irt-fall-2027")
check_material("irt-fall-2027")                # checks every lab before class does
```

See [The instructor toolkit](instructor-toolkit.html). If you use Claude or
an OpenAI assistant, the [MCP server](instructor-mcp.html) lets it revise and
adapt these materials for you.

## Also for your course

- [The book](../book/index.html), also as PDF and EPUB, with its own DOI
  ([10.5281/zenodo.23885605](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23885605)).
- [AI in measurement](ai-hub.html): Four labs and six chapters on AI for a
  later module, and a [one-day workshop kit](ai-workshop.html).
- [Glossary](glossary.html) and
  [cheat sheet](../cheatsheet/mirtverse-cheatsheet.pdf) to hand out.

## Adopting it for a course?

[Adopt mirtverse for your course](adopt.html) has a sample syllabus to edit
(Word and PDF), a setup checklist, and a two-minute form to tell us about
your course. Hearing which courses use the materials shapes what comes next.
